title: Firefighter arrested after viral video shows rifle at pool party
text:
Police say an Irving firefighter was arrested after a viral video showed him with a rifle at a neighborhood pool party. See what happened.
Video viewed millions of times shows armed confrontation near children at birthday party; firefighter placed on leave as family raises concerns at city council meeting.
A confrontation at a North Texas neighborhood pool party, captured on video and viewed millions of times online, has led to the arrest of an Irving firefighter. Police say 44-year-old Kevin Brown brought a rifle to a community pool during a dispute involving children at a birthday party. NBC 5’s Meredith Yeomans speaks with a father who witnessed the tense encounter firsthand.
A confrontation at a neighborhood pool party in North Texas, now viewed millions of times online, has led to the arrest of an Irving firefighter. Melissa police say 44-year-old Kevin Brown was arrested after bringing a rifle to a community pool during a dispute involving children at a birthday party Friday in the Meadow Run neighborhood.
Viral cellphone video captured the tense moments, including one person exclaiming, “I can’t believe this man got a gun,” as children and parents reacted to the scene. Police identified the man in the video as Brown, an Irving firefighter who lives near the neighborhood pool. Wade Simpson, a father whose daughter attended the birthday party, said he rushed to the pool after learning something had gone wrong.
“Then all of a sudden I look up and I see all the kids running frantically, and I see the guy coming with this AR-style weapon,” Wade Simpson said. “I jumped in my truck. I get down there. My daughter is trembling.
She’s trembling in fear,” Simpson said. According to Kevin Brown’s arrest affidavit, the confrontation began after Brown’s wife"spoke to children about propping open the gate to the pool and an argument ensued between her and the children’s parents. ”“I mean the whole group was going at it. It was maybe like eight people involved, shouting and things of that nature,” Simpson said.
The affidavit states a call from Brown’s wife “prompted him to come to the pool armed with an AR-platform weapon. ” “Mr. Brown decided to take an AK or AR-style weapon, walk down to a swimming pool full of babies because his wife got a consequence for bullying children,” Wade Brown said. Melissa police say Brown was initially charged with a Class C misdemeanor.
After reviewing reports, police upgraded the charge to a Class B misdemeanor for displaying a firearm in a public place. Jail records show Brown was arrested Tuesday and remained in the Collin County jail Wednesday night. Still, Simpson says the encounter reignited broader concerns for his family. Tuesday night, he addressed the Melissa City Council, speaking publicly about the incident and what he described as ongoing concerns about racism in the community.
“I would say Melissa is not a safe place for person of color,” he told NBC 5. In a statement, the Irving Fire Department said Brown has been placed on administrative leave pending what it described as a detailed internal investigation.
“Community trust is something our profession takes very seriously and will not compromise on,” the department said. “They’re going to remember this when they’re 25, 26 years old. They’re going to remember what happened in Meadow Run that day,” he said. For parents who were there, the lasting image remains the same: children running as a man carrying a rifle approached a neighborhood pool party.
